claims.claim: **Most accidental paediatric ingestions are well below a toxic dose**, but ⚠️ **a handful of agents are dangerous after 1 or 2 dose units or a mouthful** and demand a cautious risk assessment.
claims.source_text: Most accidental paediatric drug ingestions involve doses that fall well below what would be considered a toxic ingestion. There are a handful of drugs and chemicals that are dangerous after relatively small paediatric ingestions involving 1 or 2 dose units of an available preparation or a mouthful. These agents demand a cautious approach to risk assessment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'High risk - low dose paediatric ingestions' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/High_risk_-_low_dose_paediatric_ingestions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Admit for observation if there is any concern that a small child may have ingested one of these.** **Discuss all cases** with a senior clinician, Poisons Information or a clinical toxicologist. PIPER: 1300 137 650.
claims.source_text: Admission for observation is mandated if there is any concern that a small child may have ingested one of these drugs or chemicals. All cases should be discussed with a senior clinician / Poisons Information / clinical toxicologist. For emergency advice and paediatric or neonatal ICU transfers, call the Paediatric Infant Perinatal Emergency Retrieval (PIPER) Service: 1300 137 650.
